nodes.label: All Mocks No Double Counting and Derived Provenance
nodes.norm_label: all mocks no double counting and derived provenance
nodes.rationale: - A full mock is never counted again as four subject rows or two section rows in All Mocks. Derived sections sum their child results and do not inherit the parent score override, rank, percentile, or overall time.

nodes.label: Authoritative Server Sign In and Error Callback
nodes.norm_label: authoritative server sign in and error callback
nodes.rationale: The public `/sign-in` route performs an authoritative server-side `requireUser()` check with cookie caching disabled and redirects an already verified account to `/dashboard`; the client Google control only starts OAuth or offers a fallback workspace link after its own session hook resolves. nodes.label: Branch Specific Google Redirect URI

nodes.rationale: - **Todo assistance**: available from Personal todos and the AI panel. Review selectable proposals to create, edit, reschedule, complete/reopen, or move personal todos to Trash. Edit proposed details and compare existing versus proposed values before applying. Generation never saves records. Apply is transactional, version-checked, user-scoped, and idempotent; stale targets require refreshed review. Foreign record IDs return the same 404 as nonexistent IDs. Personalized responses and downloads use `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. Sign-out, session failures, and account changes unmount private dashboard state.

nodes.label: SHA 256 Preview Fingerprint
nodes.rationale: - A SHA-256 preview fingerprint covers destination content, incoming content, current/incoming target, mode, and `applyTarget`. Commits with a stale fingerprint return 409.

nodes.label: Nullable Evidence Based Extraction Draft
nodes.rationale: - **Extraction contract**: `src/lib/ai/extraction.ts` returns an editable, nullable draft with reported evidence, deterministic derived-field markers, and field-level issues—not raw `AttemptInput`. Missing values remain distinct from explicit zero. Only a blocker-free user-reviewed draft converts to `AttemptInput`; the form remains the sole save path and sets `source: "paste"`.

nodes.label: Read Only Coaching and Sole MockForm Save
nodes.norm_label: read only coaching and sole mockform save
nodes.rationale: - **Read-only guarantee**: AI routes never call repository writes. Only `MockForm` save creates attempts. Coach/chat read; extraction returns a draft that the user must explicitly apply.

nodes.label: Safe External Links and Client Confirmed AI Drafts
nodes.norm_label: safe external links and client confirmed ai drafts
nodes.rationale: - Personal tasks carry an optional external link validated by `safeHttpUrl` (strict http(s) only; empty → null). `safeHttpUrlCore` lives in the client-safe `view-model.ts` and is re-exported wrapped in zod by server-only `progress.ts` — do not duplicate the policy. Links render as `target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"` anchors with the host shown. Display status derives `overdue` via `effectiveStatus()` (completed is never overdue); the dot mapping lives in `plan-shared.tsx` `STATUS_META` and uses only theme-protected semantic tokens. AI task suggestions (`src/lib/ai/task-suggestion.ts`) are a prompt-convention fenced block parsed client-side; **AI task creation is client-confirmed — the model never writes, and the task persists only on the user's Add click.** The AI panel's Log a Mock tab never saves either: it hands a reviewed draft through `AddMockView prefill` → `MockForm initialDraft` (applied once via the same `applyExtracted` merge path), keeping `MockForm` the sole save path.

nodes.label: Abortable Parallel Workspace Refresh
nodes.rationale: - `refresh()` fetches filtered attempts, analytics, and the unfiltered list in parallel (the two attempt fetches share one request while no filter is set), aborts superseded requests, and does NOT refetch settings or AI status — those load once and reload on explicit actions only.

nodes.label: No Zustand or TanStack Query Decision
nodes.norm_label: no zustand or tanstack query decision
nodes.rationale: - **Client-state decision (2026-10 overhaul):** no Zustand and no TanStack Query. All shared client state is owned by the shell-scoped hooks above (the shell never unmounts inside the workspace, so there is no cross-component sync problem for a store to solve), server data is fetched with plain `api()` + SWR headers, and the only cross-branch contexts are `ToastProvider` and `ThemeStyleProvider`. Revisit only if a feature introduces genuinely global client state or polling/infinite-scroll server state. Cache policies: `docs/caching.md`.

nodes.label: Shell Scoped Client State Hooks
nodes.rationale: - `src/components/workspace-shell.tsx` is the client orchestrator (mounted by the `(workspace)` layout, view derived from pathname). Its state lives in three dedicated hooks — keep responsibilities there, not in the shell:

nodes.label: AES 256 GCM Credential Storage
nodes.rationale: - Keys are encrypted with AES-256-GCM under `AI_CREDENTIAL_SECRET` (`crypto-core.ts` is testable; `crypto.ts` is the `server-only` entry) into `AiCredential.apiKeyEnc`. The plaintext never leaves the server: `AiCredentialSummary` deliberately has no `apiKey` field and the only display value is a 4-character `keyHint`. `AiCredential` is never read by backups.

nodes.label: Per User Credential Resolution
nodes.rationale: - **Per-user credentials (web-configured)**: users may enter their own provider, base URL, model, and key in the UI (`AiSettingsForm`, rendered in Settings → AI provider and inside the AI Sheet when unconfigured). `src/lib/ai/resolve.ts` resolves per request: the user's stored credential wins, then the server env is the fallback; `source: "user" | "env"` drives quota (the deployment's `AI_DAILY_*` caps apply to the shared env key only).

nodes.label: Provider Endpoint SSRF Defense and DNS Rebinding Limit
nodes.norm_label: provider endpoint ssrf defense and dns rebinding limit
nodes.rationale: - Because the base URL is user-controlled, `src/lib/ai/ssrf-core.ts` blocks loopback, RFC1918, link-local/metadata (`169.254.169.254`), CGNAT, multicast, and reserved ranges plus the equivalent IPv6 forms; `ssrf.ts` adds a DNS resolution check that runs **immediately before every provider call** (save-time shape validation alone cannot see `host -> 10.0.0.5`). Each resolved address must be public. `redirect: "error"` stays on the fetch. Residual risk: DNS rebinding between our check and the provider's own resolution is not fully closed without IP pinning — do not describe it as complete.

nodes.label: Aggregate and Latest Twenty Full Mock Privacy
nodes.norm_label: aggregate and latest twenty full mock privacy
nodes.rationale: - **Context privacy**: `listAttemptsForAi` in `src/lib/repository.ts` uses Prisma `omit: { notes: true }`; `src/lib/ai/context.ts` whitelists aggregates, subjects/sections, target, and the latest 20 full mocks. It must never include notes, names, IDs, email, user ID, source, or per-attempt detail outside those latest 20 full mocks. `AnalyticsAttempt = Omit<Attempt, "notes">` is the widened analytics input type.

nodes.label: Guarded NDJSON AI Routes
nodes.rationale: - **Routes**: `/api/ai/status`, `/api/ai/coach`, `/api/ai/chat` (NDJSON stream: `start`, `delta`, `done`, `error`), `/api/ai/extract`. All use `requireUser()`, `private, no-store`, and the normal `{data}`/`{error}` envelope before streaming. AI errors are mapped in `apiError` before the Prisma fallback, so they never become `DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE`.

nodes.label: IST Daily AI Usage Reservation Ledger
nodes.norm_label: ist daily ai usage reservation ledger
nodes.rationale: - **Quota**: `AiUsage` is an app-owned ledger (`userId`, IST `day`, feature, model, tokens, status, safe error code). `reserveAiUsage` checks request/token caps in a serializable transaction before context work; `settleAiUsage` is idempotent and charges conservatively after provider errors/aborts. The reservation transaction sets `maxWait: 10s` / `timeout: 15s`; Prisma's 2s default surfaces as P2028 on a cold Neon connection. Usage rows never contain prompts, responses, notes, or report text and are excluded from backups.

nodes.label: Dedicated Personal Workspace and Forty Two Day Summary
nodes.norm_label: dedicated personal workspace and forty two day summary
nodes.rationale: - `/my-tasks` opens `PersonalTodos` directly; `/calendar` is study-plan focused. Personal lists preserve groups, subtasks, Trash, and legacy undated records. `/api/todos/calendar` aggregates per-date pending/completed counts over an inclusive maximum of 42 days, always scoped to the verified owner and excluding Trash. List pagination never limits calendar counts. No schema migration is introduced by the overhaul.

nodes.label: Overview Today Plan Study Calendar Order
nodes.norm_label: overview today plan study calendar order
nodes.rationale: - Dashboard order is Overview → Today's Plan → Study Calendar, then supporting panels and performance. Today's Plan uses today's structured assignments plus the shared personal-task workspace and an overdue preview excluding the selected personal date. Personal selection and Study Calendar selection are independent.

nodes.label: Shell Scoped Todo Query Cache
nodes.rationale: - `usePlanData` owns merged study-plan progress; `TodosDataProvider` (`use-todos-data.tsx`) owns the shell-lifetime personal-task query cache, including legacy `/api/tasks` reads, versioned todo lists, AI reference data, and calendar summaries. Identical reads share an in-flight request; `ssc:todos-changed` invalidates personal queries without refetching the static plan. Study-plan mutations remain optimistic with refetch on failure. Views: `plan/calendar-view.tsx`, `plan/tasks-view.tsx`, `plan/plan-day-view.tsx`, `plan/dashboard-plan-sections.tsx`; `/plan/<date>` is matched by prefix in the shell's view derivation.

nodes.norm_label: aggregate and latest twenty full mock privacy
nodes.rationale: - Ordinary coaching context is limited to aggregate analytics and the latest 20 full mocks. Mock notes, email, user identity, auth data, and per-attempt detail outside those latest 20 full mocks are never sent. The pasted report is sent only for extraction and is treated as untrusted data.

nodes.label: Analytical Scope Projections Without Double Counting
nodes.norm_label: analytical scope projections without double counting
nodes.rationale: - Dashboard tabs switch the analytical grain rather than filtering the saved-record table. Full Mocks projects saved full mocks. Subject Wise projects every subject result from full, sectional, and standalone subject mocks, with all subjects shown together. Sectional Wise projects explicit sectionals plus Section I (Quant + Reasoning) and Section II (English + General Awareness) derived from each full mock. All Mocks projects every saved attempt exactly once and compares percentages across different maxima. A full mock is not additionally counted as its subjects or sections in All Mocks.

nodes.label: Atomic Merge and Confirmed Replace Import
nodes.norm_label: atomic merge and confirmed replace import
nodes.rationale: - Preview an import with merge or replace modes. Merge preserves existing records and skips exact duplicates while reporting content conflicts; replace deletes the current account’s mocks after an explicit safety-backup download and confirmation naming the signed-in account. All imports are atomic.

nodes.label: Attempt Scheduled and Recorded Date Semantics
nodes.norm_label: attempt scheduled and recorded date semantics
nodes.rationale: - Attempt dates are distinct from scheduled dates and from recording time. The form labels the field "Attempt date", defaults to today in IST, and the actual attempt date is what history, charts, and date filters use. A mock attempted on a different day than scheduled appears on the day it was actually attempted.

nodes.label: Daily Study Workspace
nodes.rationale: - A daily workspace at /plan/<date> lists the day's assignments with completion, result recording (score, percentile, wrong, unattempted — blank stays unknown), the four daily-checklist habits, the day's revision blocks, and weak-area notes. It also lists the tracker attempts logged for that date.

nodes.label: Date Only Logging and Summed Duration
nodes.norm_label: date only logging and summed duration
nodes.rationale: - Log a date without a time, choose a platform preset or enter a custom platform, and enter durations using three hour/minute/second blocks. Scores update live from question counts; overall time is calculated automatically. Empty time blocks become zero.

nodes.label: Dated Personal Tasks Groups Subtasks Filters Sorting
nodes.norm_label: dated personal tasks groups subtasks filters sorting
nodes.rationale: - Personal todos require a date (no time), with quick title entry, optional notes and priority, reusable groups, and subtasks sharing the parent date. Month browsing and Selected day/Today/Overdue/Upcoming/All/Completed views support paginated lists, search, status/group/priority filters, and priority/date/newest/title sorting. Legacy undated tasks remain in Needs date until assigned a date. Every personal task may carry one optional external link: it is validated to strict http(s), always opens in a new tab with the destination host shown, and never auto-opens.

nodes.label: Dedicated Personal Task Workspace
nodes.rationale: - My Tasks opens directly into the full personal-task workspace, with a month calendar, selected-date list, quick entry, editing, rescheduling, groups, filters, and sorting. The Study Calendar focuses on structured assignments and scheduled mocks. Personal dates are not limited to the mock-plan window.

nodes.label: Explicitly Reviewed Versioned AI Todo Proposals
nodes.norm_label: explicitly reviewed versioned ai todo proposals
nodes.rationale: - Todo assistance in the personal planner and AI panel generates selectable, editable proposals for creation, editing, rescheduling, completion/reopening, or moving to Trash. The user must provide a date or range, review before/after values, then explicitly apply selected changes. Generation itself never mutates data; server-side ownership, record versions, and idempotency protect apply/retry behavior. AI-proposed todos carrying a link are held to the same strict http(s) policy.

nodes.label: Four MB Account Transfer Boundary
nodes.rationale: - Imports have a 4 MB transport limit. The app does not change the Google login identity and never reassigns ownership server-side; moving to a different Google account means exporting there and importing here.

nodes.label: Full Sectional Subject and Computer Scoring
nodes.norm_label: full sectional subject and computer scoring
nodes.rationale: - Track full mocks, single-subject mocks, and sectional mocks. Full mocks contain Quant, Reasoning, English, and General Awareness with a maximum of 390 marks. Computer Knowledge can optionally be included with a full mock and is scored separately; its time contributes to the overall time. It can also be logged as a standalone subject.

nodes.label: Global Radar and Score Centered Outcome Cards
nodes.norm_label: global radar and score centered outcome cards
nodes.rationale: - Where you stand is one global subject radar on every tab. Make every attempt count uses reference-led visual outcome cards for the selected analytical grain: one Full Mocks card, one card per populated subject or section, and parent attempts grouped by mock type in All Mocks. Every card shows attempt/question coverage, score percentage, Correct/Incorrect/Unattempted counts and shares, and aggregate marks/max, with a score-centered answer ring, answer-share bars, accuracy, and explicit reported-percentile availability—without percentile borrowing or extra projections. Subject deep dive appears on every tab except Subject Wise.

nodes.label: History Comparison and URL Mirrored Filters
nodes.norm_label: history comparison and url mirrored filters
nodes.rationale: - Review history using type, subject, platform, date, and text filters. Compare two to four attempts, using percentages where maximum marks differ. Active filters and the dashboard scope are mirrored into the page address, so a bookmarked or shared link restores the same filtered view after signing in; browser Back moves between pages, not between filter states.

nodes.label: Immutable Fifty Day RBE Study Plan
nodes.norm_label: immutable fifty day rbe study plan
nodes.rationale: - Follow a built-in 50-day study plan (26 Oct – 14 Dec 2026, three phases) imported from the RBE daily-targets PDF. The plan itself is read-only source data; the student's completions, recorded results, revision flags, checklist, and notes are stored separately per account.

nodes.label: Independent Personal and Study Calendars
nodes.rationale: - A study calendar covers the whole plan window with month, week, day, and agenda views; every scheduled test keeps its original RBE link. Selecting a date reveals that day's schedule; /plan/<date> is the shareable deep link. Personal tasks have independent calendars in My Tasks and the dashboard; their selection never changes the Study Calendar.

nodes.label: Invoked Todo Assistance Expanded Context Disclosure
nodes.norm_label: invoked todo assistance expanded context disclosure
nodes.rationale: - Todo assistance may send a bounded set of active personal todo titles, dates, statuses, notes, and subtasks, plus aggregate mock performance and the requested study-plan window, to the configured provider. This expanded context is confined to todo assistance, excludes Trash and account identity, and is disclosed before generation. Existing coaching privacy scope stays unchanged.

nodes.label: Isolated Google Signed In Accounts
nodes.rationale: SSC aspirants sign in with Google and work in isolated private accounts. Each user can access and change only their own mocks and settings. Anonymous visitors must sign in before entering the dashboard.

nodes.label: IST Daily AI Usage Caps
nodes.rationale: - Every request is subject to an IST-daily request and token cap. Usage rows log feature, model, token counts, status, and safe error codes, but never prompts, responses, notes, or report text.

nodes.label: Manually Generated Coach Insight
nodes.rationale: - The coach card is generated manually, not on page load. It returns a structured headline, summary, strengths, focus areas, next actions, and caveats.

nodes.label: Next React Prisma Neon Implementation
nodes.rationale: Next.js 16 App Router with React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, shadcn-style Radix button and dialog primitives, Motion, and Recharts. Persistence uses Prisma 7 with Neon PostgreSQL, dedicated schema `ssc_insight`, in project `lingering-mode-47457333`, production branch. Neon Auth manages Google sessions separately. An optional server-side AI layer uses an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint; ordinary coaching is read-only, and the separate todo mode proposes explicitly reviewed personal-task mutations. Both are available when a user credential or server configuration is present. The migration starts empty and leaves Firebase data untouched. Database setup and credentials belong to deployment configuration, not client code or design documentation.

nodes.label: Nullable Reviewed Extraction Draft
nodes.rationale: - AI-assisted paste returns an editable draft that distinguishes reported values, safely derived SSC counts, and missing fields. The user reviews or corrects mock details, subject counts, timings, rank, and percentile before choosing **Use reviewed values**; saving remains the existing separate form action. Contradictions and required missing values block copying, while the deterministic paste parser stays available as a fallback.

nodes.label: Optional OpenAI Compatible AI Provider
nodes.rationale: AI is optional and uses an OpenAI-compatible endpoint configured by the user or through server defaults. When it is unavailable, the tracker remains fully usable and the AI card and assisted-extraction action are hidden or disabled.

nodes.label: Overview Today Plan Study Calendar Sequence
nodes.norm_label: overview today plan study calendar sequence
nodes.rationale: - The dashboard shows Overview, Today's Plan, then Study Calendar. Today's Plan combines today's study assignments with personal tasks, a personal mini-calendar, and a distinct overdue preview excluding the selected date. Selecting a personal date changes only personal work; study assignments stay anchored to today. Plan progress, upcoming tests, revisions, recent attempts, coaching, and performance follow these primary sections. Revision completion remains manual.

nodes.label: Parent Subtask Completion and Derived Overdue
nodes.norm_label: parent subtask completion and derived overdue
nodes.rationale: - Unfinished todos stay on their original dates and become overdue. Within date/group, unfinished items appear first by priority, followed by completed items. Checking a parent completes all its subtasks; unchecking it reopens them all. Completing all subtasks completes the parent, and reopening one reopens the parent. Task status is shown with status dots (todo, in progress, done, derived overdue) that follow the app's semantic tokens — identical across every palette and style.

nodes.label: Performance Analytics and Unknown Values
nodes.rationale: - See score trends, question breakdowns, subject strengths, accuracy, timing, and target progress. Missing values remain unknown rather than becoming zero.

nodes.label: Portable Identity Free JSON Backup
nodes.rationale: - Download a portable JSON backup containing all mocks, subject results, notes, ranks/percentiles, timings, overrides, source metadata, and the target score. The file excludes email, user IDs, and credentials, so it can be imported into a different signed-in account.

nodes.label: Private SSC Insight Mock Tracker
nodes.rationale: SSC Insight is a personal SSC CGL Tier 2 mock tracker. It helps an aspirant record results, understand performance over time, and decide what to practice next. The public `/` route explains the product; verified accounts redirect to `/dashboard`, and `/sign-in` handles account access.

nodes.label: Read Only Coaching Versus Reviewed Todo Mutation
nodes.norm_label: read only coaching versus reviewed todo mutation
nodes.rationale: - Ordinary coaching and report extraction have no write tools. Todo assistance is a separate mode: it proposes personal-todo operations, and only explicit reviewed confirmation invokes the apply endpoint. Mock records and built-in study-plan assignments cannot be AI mutation targets. Prompt-injected instructions never authorize changes.

nodes.label: Read Only CSV and Legacy V1 Imports
nodes.norm_label: read only csv and legacy v1 imports
nodes.rationale: - CSV remains a read-only spreadsheet export and cannot be imported. Legacy version-1 backups remain importable; the target is unavailable in them.

nodes.label: Read Only Session Coach Context
nodes.rationale: - Generate an optional AI coaching read of saved performance and ask follow-up questions in a session-only chat panel. The panel knows which screen and plan date you are viewing (shown as a small context chip) but receives no attempt details beyond the standard analysis context. The coach is read-only; it never creates, edits, deletes, or schedules records.

nodes.label: Recoverable Trash and Ungrouped Restoration
nodes.rationale: - Deleting a personal todo moves it and its subtasks to recoverable Trash; no automatic expiry or permanent deletion is provided. Restoring keeps its original date/details/completion state. Deleting a group preserves todos as Ungrouped, including restoration when the old group is gone. Personal todos never alter mock attempts or built-in plan assignments.

nodes.label: Result Tracker Scope Boundaries
nodes.rationale: This is a result tracker, not an exam-taking platform, coaching marketplace, marketing landing page, or account-management product. The AI coach is an optional in-app analysis aid, not a marketplace, tutor, or autonomous agent. Backup restoration supports reviewed merge and explicit replace; replacement is never silent and requires a current safety backup and confirmation naming the signed-in account.

nodes.label: Reviewable Mock CRUD
nodes.rationale: - Log, edit, inspect, and delete mock attempts with platform, date, subject breakdown, optional timing, rank, percentile, and notes.

nodes.label: Session Failure Privacy Boundary
nodes.rationale: Google sign-in is required. Each user owns their mocks, analytics, comparisons, backups, and target setting. All data APIs verify the session and scope database queries by its user ID. There are no guest records, shared settings, or administrator views. Session failure hides private content, and account changes remount the workspace.

nodes.label: Session Only In Memory Chat
nodes.rationale: - Follow-up chat is session-only and held in memory; it disappears on reload, sign-out, account change, or session failure. It is never written to browser storage.

nodes.label: Single Percentage Target
nodes.rationale: - Set one target score out of 390 and use it as a percentage reference on every dashboard tab.

nodes.label: Sole Mock Form Save and Planner Handoff
nodes.norm_label: sole mock form save and planner handoff
nodes.rationale: - Every planner surface offers an Add mock record action that opens the normal mock form prefilled with the selected attempt date (and the scheduled test's name when started from a task). Saving records a normal tracker attempt on its own attempt date. It never creates, moves, or auto-completes a scheduled plan item, and a plan task's own result fields remain the explicit way to record plan progress.

nodes.label: Three Mode AI Panel
nodes.rationale: - The AI panel has three tabs. **Coach chat** renders answers with light formatting (headings, bold, inline code, bullets, code blocks, bare links shown as host-labeled anchors) plus a Copy action per answer. **Log a mock** reuses the paste-extraction flow: paste a scorecard, parse it with AI (or the deterministic parser when AI is off), review the draft inline, and continue to the real form with every reviewed value prefilled — the panel itself never saves. **Plan todos** hosts the todo-assistance composer. Ad-hoc task requests in chat produce a suggestion card (title, due date, priority, category, notes, optional https link) that persists only when the user clicks **Add task**; a non-http link is stripped from the card with a warning. The coach never claims a task was saved.

nodes.label: User Configured Provider Model Discovery and Draft Test
nodes.norm_label: user configured provider model discovery and draft test
nodes.rationale: - Configure the AI provider yourself from Settings → AI provider, or directly inside the AI panel when it is not yet set up. Choose a preset (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, Together, DeepSeek, or a local Ollama) or a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint, enter an API key, then fetch, search, and select a model from the provider’s catalog. An exact model ID can also be entered manually. Test the draft connection before saving; the test sends one small completion, may incur a small provider charge, and does not save changes. A key you enter is encrypted before it is stored, is never shown back to you (only its last four characters), is never written to a backup, and can be removed at any time. Leaving the key blank reuses a saved key only for the same provider and endpoint; changing either requires a new key. Model discovery and draft testing run on the server without persisting the draft. The server may also provide a shared configuration, which yours takes precedence over.

nodes.label: User Reviewed Report Extraction
nodes.rationale: - Paste a result report into a reviewable form before saving; preserve manual correction and explicit review. An optional AI helper can arrange the pasted report into a draft, but the user must apply it and review every field before saving.

nodes.label: Warm Editorial Paper Product Principles
nodes.rationale: Keep logging quick and analysis readable. Use calm, direct language and a warm paper workspace with editorial typography, thin rules, clear tables, charts, and empty states. Dates are displayed in India Standard Time. Scores and percentages must retain their underlying meaning across different mock types.

nodes.label: Paper Ink Typography Design References
nodes.rationale: Cream paper, charcoal ink, Source Serif 4 headings, DM Sans controls, square panels, and terracotta actions. See [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) and [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md).

nodes.label: Authenticated JSON Envelope API Contract
nodes.rationale: Routes retain `{data}` / `{error: {code, message}}` response envelopes, validation, same-origin writes, and request-size limits. JSON backups and CSV use downloadable responses.

nodes.label: Read Only AI Todo Proposal API
nodes.norm_label: read only ai todo proposal api
nodes.rationale: | `/api/ai/todos` | POST | Ask for missing dates or generate bounded personal-todo proposals and before snapshots; never applies changes |

nodes.label: Versioned Todo Edit Restore and Trash API
nodes.norm_label: versioned todo edit restore and trash api
nodes.rationale: | `/api/todos/:id` | PATCH, DELETE | Version-checked edits, completion/subtasks, restoration, or soft deletion to Trash |

nodes.label: Cascading SubjectResult Ownership
nodes.rationale: - `SubjectResult` — child rows keyed by `(attemptId, subjectId)`; ownership cascades from the attempt.

nodes.label: Owned MockAttempt
nodes.rationale: - `MockAttempt` — one saved attempt: type, date, optional overrides, rank/participants/percentile, notes, source, owner `userId`.

nodes.label: Central API Safety Envelope
nodes.rationale: - `src/lib/api.ts` centralizes `{ data }` / `{ error: { code, message } }`, `private, no-store`, same-origin write checks, JSON/body size limits, and Prisma error mapping. The backup GET is the exception: it returns a raw downloadable file.

nodes.label: Foreign and Missing IDs Share 404
nodes.rationale: - Foreign and nonexistent record IDs intentionally return the same 404.

nodes.label: Derived SSC Plus Three Minus One Scoring
nodes.norm_label: derived ssc plus three minus one scoring
nodes.rationale: - Scoring is +3 correct / −1 incorrect. `subjectStats()` and `totals()` derive scores, accuracy, percentages, skipped counts, and time. Do not persist derived values.

nodes.label: Full Mock Computer Exclusion
nodes.rationale: - Full mocks: the four main subjects with fixed counts (30/30/45/25), maximum 390. Optional Computer is scored separately and excluded from full totals, but its time contributes to overall time.

nodes.label: Five Palettes Three Styles
nodes.rationale: - **Multi-theme system:** `data-palette` (orange=original default, blue, lime, violet, rose) and `data-style` (vega=original default, sera, mira) are `<html>` attributes set before paint by the inline script in `theme-style-provider.tsx` (localStorage `ssc.palette`/`ssc.style`, safe defaults) and resolved entirely by CSS custom properties in `globals.css` — never hardcode palette hexes in components. Chart hues alias `--accent`/`--muted` where the identity is shared; per-palette chart hues live in the `[data-palette]` blocks. Styles vary geometry/density/motion via tokens (`--radius-*`, `--control-*`, `--table-cell-*`, `--dur-*`, `--elev-pop`); density vars are consumed by the base element defaults and component classes, so Tailwind utilities still override per view. The selection UI is `appearance-panel.tsx` in Settings (choices apply instantly, aria-pressed, mounted-gated selected states). next-themes keeps owning light/dark; each palette defines its own dark charcoal tint in `.dark[data-palette=…]`. All 15 combinations keep AA accent contrast (verified) and identical layout/behavior.

nodes.label: Semantic Paper Ink Chart Tokens
nodes.rationale: - `src/app/globals.css` + `src/lib/chart-theme.ts` define paper/ink/accent and semantic chart tokens. Preserve them. Shadcn-only aliases (`--background`, `--border`, `--sidebar-*`, …) map onto those tokens; `--accent` stays terracotta and is never repurposed as shadcn's neutral hover. `tw-animate-css` is not installed, so the Sheet/tooltip primitives use local `data-state` CSS (`sheet-overlay`, `sheet-content`) with the existing duration/easing tokens instead of generated `animate-in` utilities.

nodes.label: Google Neon Auth Account Isolation
nodes.rationale: - Auth uses Neon Auth with Google. The app stores no email/user row and has no ownership relation to Neon Auth tables. A different Google account is a separate workspace. Do not write to `neon_auth` or add a server-side owner-reassignment endpoint.

nodes.label: Verified Session Derived Ownership
nodes.rationale: - Ownership is always the verified Neon Auth user ID from `requireUser()`. Never accept `userId` from a body, query, or backup.

nodes.label: Immutable Fifty Day Study Schedule
nodes.rationale: The 50-day plan is static source data (`src/data/study-plan.json`, zod-validated in `src/lib/plan/schema.ts`; note the export declares 273 tests but contains 262 — counts always derive from actual rows). User progress lives in `PlanTaskProgress` / `PlanDayProgress` / `PersonalTask` (migration `20261027000000_study_planner`), keyed by deterministic plan identities (`taskKey = d{day}:{taskIndex}`, plan day number) — completing work never rewrites the schedule, and there is no seed or duplicate-row risk.

nodes.label: Owned Plan Progress Routes
nodes.rationale: - `src/lib/plan/progress.ts` merges plan × progress and owns all mutations. Routes: `GET /api/plan` (merged payload), `POST /api/plan/progress` (zod discriminated union: task patch / checklist / day revision / day notes), `GET|POST /api/tasks`, `PUT|DELETE /api/tasks/[id]` — all through `defineRoute` with ownership scoping like every other route.

nodes.label: In Memory Conversation and Abort Lifetime
nodes.norm_label: in memory conversation and abort lifetime
nodes.rationale: - **UI state**: the coach card is presentational; status, insight, chat messages, and the abort controller live in `use-ai-workspace.ts` so they survive view switches. Chat is in-memory only — no sessionStorage/localStorage, and closing the Sheet never clears messages. The hook aborts in-flight streams on close/unmount. AI controls are hidden/disabled when unconfigured.

nodes.label: Three Mode Responsive AI Sheet
nodes.rationale: - The AI panel is a right-side shadcn Sheet (`ai-chat-sheet.tsx`, desktop ~520px, full width on mobile, `dvh` flex layout with an independently scrolling log, compact tabs: Coach chat / Plan todos / Log a mock; visual-viewport and safe-area composer sizing). Chat accepts a validated orientation-only screen context (`{ view, date? }`, wrapped as `<screen_context>` in the system prompt); it carries no titles, notes, IDs, email, or attempt records.

nodes.label: Independent Route Authentication
nodes.rationale: - Route handlers authenticate independently; page middleware (`src/proxy.ts`) covers only pages.

nodes.label: Private No Store Account Data
nodes.rationale: - Cache Components are not enabled. Personalized APIs use `Cache-Control: private, no-store`; do not add shared caching or `revalidate` behavior to account data.

nodes.rationale: DESIGN.md mandates square corners but reality was mixed (rounded-2xl maintenance page, 10px outcome cards, 4px skeletons, pill landing tiles) with no tokens, so the 'moderately rounded corners' directive had to be satisfied by a tokenized radius scale on controls rather than by rounding structural geometry.

nodes.label: Elevation Model and --shadow-pop Token
nodes.rationale: Depth is flat at level 0 via rules and surface change; the single lifted token is ink-tinted (never gray-on-cream) and reserved for popovers, toasts, dialogs, and command surfaces, with hover lift done by rule darkening plus 2px translate instead of shadows.

nodes.label: Restrained Motion Language
nodes.rationale: 140ms hover, 220ms enter, 240ms view switch with no horizontal slides, 70ms stagger capped at 6 children and only once; charts never animate and every new path must be reduced-motion aware.

nodes.label: Tokenized Radius Scale (panel/control/card/pill)
nodes.rationale: 0px for panels/stat strip/tables/dialogs/nav preserves the ledger identity, 4px belongs to controls, 10px to expressive cards, and pills only to dots and bars — tokens rather than per-component guesswork.

nodes.label: Sticky Identity Column for Mock History
nodes.norm_label: sticky identity column for mock history
nodes.rationale: At 375px the ledger's remaining columns scroll while the mock name stays pinned, so a row stays identifiable; verified by scrolling 220px.

nodes.label: Paper-and-Ink Design System
nodes.rationale: Warm editorial paper (cream canvas, paper surfaces, serif headings, terracotta actions, thin rules) chosen for the clarity of a printed progress ledger; Anthropic was a visual reference, not a brand identity to reproduce.

nodes.label: Handover Conventions to Keep
nodes.rationale: Identity is the ledger (structural geometry square, 4px controls, 10px expressive cards), one segmented-control pattern, all icons through icon.tsx, semantic accuracy color always paired with the printed value, deployment-neutral copy — so future features cannot erode the overhaul.

nodes.label: "The Printed Progress Ledger" Design Direction
nodes.rationale: Product personality is a calm editorial workspace treating exam prep as a record worth keeping: every addition must feel typeset, not decorated, which is why structural geometry stays square and palette/chart hues are frozen.

nodes.label: Request and Ownership Architecture
nodes.rationale: Ownership is always the verified Neon Auth user ID from requireUser(); a userId from body, query, or backup is never accepted, and foreign vs nonexistent IDs both return 404 so ID probing reveals nothing.

nodes.label: Neon Agent Tooling Setup (Codex plugin + MCP)
nodes.norm_label: neon agent tooling setup (codex plugin + mcp)
nodes.rationale: The bundled neon-postgres plugin already ships the Neon skills and the OAuth MCP server, so no duplicate standalone skills/MCP entries were added; CLI operations were preferred, and a failed unrelated Copilot installer was bypassed with --agent codex.

nodes.label: Expiring QA Branch Migration Rehearsal
nodes.rationale: The reviewed initial migration ran on an expiring branch first and only then on production, so a broken migration could not damage real data.

nodes.label: Private-Accounts Migration (claim two shared mocks)
nodes.rationale: The migration only targets ssc_insight, reads the managed Auth table to find exactly one email-verified identity, aborts on any unexpected nonzero mock count, and never claims records for the first visitor.

nodes.label: Session-Derived Ownership Model
nodes.rationale: Every data route verifies Neon Auth independently and bypasses the SDK's five-minute cookie cache so revoked sessions cannot authorize requests, even though that costs a verification call per request.

nodes.label: Google Sign-In via Neon Auth OAuth
nodes.norm_label: google sign-in via neon auth oauth
nodes.rationale: The callback registered with Google is {NEON_AUTH_BASE_URL}/callback/google, not the app's /auth/complete landing, and each branch has its own Auth base URL — a common setup mistake. Server-side requireUser() is authoritative; client useSession() is only a UI fallback.

nodes.label: Verification Scripts and QA Discipline
nodes.rationale: A passing session endpoint is not proof of Google login, and destructive replace checks are gated behind ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_REPLACE because they run against real disposable accounts on a QA branch.

nodes.label: Controlled Release and Rollback Strategy
nodes.rationale: Rolling the app alone back to the public revision is unsafe and schema-incompatible, so a forward fix keeping the private guard is preferred; any destructive production restore needs a new reviewed release that preserves later private-account records.

nodes.label: Backup Format v2 and Account Transfer
nodes.norm_label: backup format v2 and account transfer
nodes.rationale: Fingerprint-gated, transactional merge/replace exist so a stale preview cannot commit; replace is double-gated (client safety download naming the account, server confirmReplace) because destructive replacement must never be silent.

nodes.label: Semantic Chart Palette and Chart Rules
nodes.norm_label: semantic chart palette and chart rules
nodes.rationale: Subject hues are a fixed categorical order validated for CVD and normal-vision separation against paper; series are never colored by value and no extra hues are cycled, so an entity keeps one color across filters. Single percentage axis, animation off, reduced motion respected.

nodes.label: JSON Backup Format Version 2
nodes.rationale: The 4 MB / 10,000-attempt cap exists to stay inside the deployment request-body limit; backups are manual only (no scheduled jobs, reminders, email, or ZIP) by product decision, and CSV stays read-only because only the versioned JSON has a lossless round-trip contract.

nodes.label: Dashboard Scope Projection Invariants
nodes.rationale: Tabs are analytical scopes, not record filters: never union projections for All Mocks (one full mock must not recount as four subjects and two sections), derived sections never inherit the parent's override/rank/percentile/time, and missing values stay null rather than zero.

nodes.label: Three Date Semantics (scheduled / attempt / recorded)
nodes.rationale: Scheduled date = plan day, attempt date = completedAt (used by filters, ordering, analytics), recorded date = createdAt shown only as 'Logged'; trend ordering uses completedAt so a late-logged mock still plots on its real attempt date.

nodes.label: Product Principles (quick logging, readable analysis)
nodes.rationale: Keep logging quick and analysis readable; uses calm direct language, warm paper with editorial typography, IST dates, and scores whose underlying meaning survives across differing mock maxima.

nodes.label: Known Limitations (duo-icons fill-rule, native inputs)
nodes.rationale: Native selects and date inputs keep platform UI deliberately for touch reliability; the duo-icons fill-rule warning is library-internal and the Recharts 0-size warning is dev-only, so neither justifies churn.

nodes.label: Icon Size Scale (14/16/18/22/28)
nodes.rationale: Duo icons first with Lucide fallback and no ad-hoc sizes; icon-only controls always carry aria-label and decorative icons aria-hidden.

nodes.label: Named Imports for Bundle Reduction
nodes.rationale: A namespace import from @duo-icons/react kept unused glyphs in the client bundle; per-glyph named imports funnel every icon through icon.tsx so unused ones drop out.

nodes.label: Raw Lucide Imports Migrated into Semantic Icon Map
nodes.norm_label: raw lucide imports migrated into semantic icon map
